name: Gorespur
body:
GORESPUR CR 1

This slavering humanoid is covered in bony protrusions and its cavernous mouth consists of rows upon rows of overlapping, sharp teeth. With a sickening snap, it extends two bony blades from its forearms as it growls in challenge.

XP 400
CE Medium monstrous humanoid
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +6

DEFENSE

AC 12, touch 11, flat-footed 11 (+1 Dex, +1 natural)
hp 15 (2d10+4)
Fort +4, Ref +4, Will +4
Defensive Abilities ferocity

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee bite +4 (1d6+2), 2 claws +4 (1d6+2)
Special Attacks rend (2 claws, 1d6+3), retractable arm-blades

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 13, Con 14, Int 8, Wis 13, Cha 6
Base Atk +2; CMB +4; CMD 15
Feats Great Fortitude
Skills Perception +6, Stealth +6, Survival +6
Languages Gorespur

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Retractable Arm-blades (Ex)

A gorespur can extend or retract its arm-blades as a swift action. A gorespur with extended arm-blades cannot use its hands to hold items, but gains two primary claw attacks (included in the statblock above). An arm-blade can be sundered or disarmed, and it is treated as a scizore for that purpose. A disarmed or sundered arm-blade is destroyed and regrows in 24 hours.

ECOLOGY

Environment any land
Organization solitary, gang (2–4), squad (5–12 plus 1 barbarian or ranger of 3rd level), or tribe (13–30 plus 1 chieftain of 7th level, 1 cleric or shaman of 5th level, and 2–4 barbarians or rangers of 3rd level)
Treasure standard

Gorespurs are tribal nomads, considered rabid monsters by most. Feral and ferocious, they are widely known as fearless and deadly combatants. Such is their fabled aggression and brutality that even most orc tribes try to steer clear of gorespur encampments, unless they are sure they can strike out at the tribe with overwhelming force and destroy it entirely before it grows or moves out of sight.

Though not the most intelligent humanoids, gorespurs are far from animals, though their culture might make others think otherwise. They live in crude tents made of animal hide and travel on foot, changing camp often. They are entirely carnivorous, and the staple of their diet comes from hunting down any beast not swift enough to outrun them. Most of them have neither patience nor skill to tame and train animals, devouring any creature they can find. They supplement this diet by raiding, as they consider the meat of most humanoids a delicacy, and such incidents are marked mostly by feast and carnage.

Gorespurs not only eat others, but also practice cannibalism. Unless the body is too disease-ridden or poisoned to eat safely, each dead gorespur is feasted upon by the tribe, and it is customary for the victor to consume the beaten opponent after a fight to the death. Those fights happen often, mostly as a matter of honor or a question of leadership, with many members of the tribe eagerly gathering to watch the entertainment. Aside from being cannibals and nomads, gorespurs are also warriors and have a strong sense of honor, although it mostly revolves around general strength and combat proficiency. A gorespur that tolerates slights or implications of his martial incompetence is seen as weak and often ostracized, with further offenses against him escalating as time passes until he leaves or is killed by his tribesmen.

The strongest gorespur, determined by combat between challengers, leads the tribe and has to die, either to foe or challenger, before that leadership changes. Leaders rarely challenge their subordinates to combat unless insulted, as that is seen as bullying and attempting to cull the tribe’s strong to unfairly prolong leadership.

Except their maws, which contain an overcrowded abundance of sharp, constantly regrowing teeth nestled in overlapping rows, the most prominent feature of gorespurs are their arm-blades, which give them their name. Each gorespur has a sharp, bony blade hidden in their arms, giving their forearms an overmuscled look. Gorespurs learn how to control these blades via muscle contractions at an early age, taking caution that the wound caused by the first emergence of the blade scars well and never fully heals. These blades are used as a primary weapon in combat, and gorespurs very rarely learn to use any manufactured weaponry, having such deadly tools of their own. Arm-blades of gorespurs are entirely organic and made of dense bone. If torn out or destroyed, the remnants of the blade are quickly absorbed by the body and a replacement grows out in about a day. This process requires a great supply of collagen and calcium, which are provided by the fact that gorespurs tend to eat their victims with all the bones included. Challenging a gorespur that lacks an arm-blade is considered dishonorable, and the challenger often waits for the arm-blade to regrow before insisting on combat.

An average gorespur is about 6 feet tall and weighs 200 pounds, with wiry muscle and leathery skin covered in sharp, bony protrusions. They very rarely have any hair, and it is considered a physical abnormality in the race. Sexual dimorphism is less pronounced than in humans, and males and females are seen as equals. Gorespurs can live to 60 years old, but most die far younger through violence.

Gorespurs advance by gaining class levels, often as barbarians or fighters, especially archetypes revolving around cannibalism or natural attacks. The tribes have few spellcasters, as arcane is distrusted and martial is expected, and only clerics and shamans are sometimes tolerated, especially those with the Cannibalism domain.

Gorespur Feats
Blade Ejection (Combat)

You have gained total control of your arm-blades, having mastered the movement of the muscles that operate them.

Prerequisites: Dex 15, gorespur.

Benefit: You can extend or retract your arm-blades as a free action. In addition, you can shoot out your arm-blade as a ranged attack with a range of 20 feet (no range increment), dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier. An arm-blade that has been shot out is treated as destroyed and regrows in 24 hours.

Gorespur Style (Combat, Style)

You call upon your inner reserves of blinding ferocity, allowing you to rip and tear with terrifying skill.

Prerequisites: One or more natural attacks, base attack bonus +6.

Benefit: When you enter this style, choose one type of natural attack you possess (bite, claws, etc.). As long as the style persists, each natural attack you possess of this specific type counts as a light manufactured weapon for the purpose of iterative attacks or two-weapon fighting. If you possess multiple natural attacks of the chosen type, they are treated as main-hand and off-hand weapons, with the appropriate penalties. Any natural attacks other than those chosen with Gorespur Style are treated as secondary natural attacks until you exit the style.

Normal: You cannot make iterative attacks with natural attacks.
